findings.title: Raw-HTML posts bypass all sanitization, enabling stored XSS from feeds/remote pages
findings.body: Post#cook returns `raw` verbatim when cook_method is raw_html, and TopicEmbed.import creates such posts from untrusted RSS/Atom content (Jobs::PollFeed) and arbitrary remote-page content extracted by Readability (TopicEmbed.import_remote). Neither path sanitizes script tags, event-handler attributes, or javascript: URLs before storage, and views output post.cooked (e.g. embed/best.html.erb uses `raw post.cooked`, and normal topic views trust cooked HTML). A malicious or compromised feed/page on the embeddable host therefore stores active HTML/JS that executes in the Discourse origin for every reader, not only in the embed iframe.

findings.title: Unescaped referer interpolated into JavaScript and used as postMessage targetOrigin
findings.body: `'<%= request.referer %>'` inserts the Referer header into a single-quoted JS string with no JavaScript/HTML escaping. A referer containing a quote or `</script>` breaks out of the string/script context and executes attacker JS in the Discourse origin inside the embed iframe. Additionally, postMessage's targetOrigin must be a serialized origin (scheme/host/port), not a full URL with a path; passing the full referer will cause browsers to drop the resize message, so legitimate resizing also fails.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses substring matching instead of origin equality
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any e.origin that happens to be a substring of discourseUrl, rather than requiring e.origin to equal the Discourse origin (scheme + host + port, with trailing slash stripped). Shortened/prefix origins therefore pass, weakening the check that is supposed to ensure only the Discourse iframe can resize the embed. Compare the normalized origin exactly instead.

findings.title: import_remote fetches arbitrary URLs server-side with open() and no timeout/validation
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import_remote does `open(url).read` on a URL ultimately derived from the user-supplied embed_url parameter (EmbedController -> Jobs::RetrieveTopic -> TopicRetriever). TopicRetriever only compares URI host to embeddable_host; there is no timeout, size limit, scheme validation inside import itself, or protection against redirects to internal addresses (open-uri follows redirects). A URL on the allowed host that redirects to an internal/metadata endpoint, or a slow/huge response, can be used for SSRF or to tie up Sidekiq workers. Validate the final URL, set open/read timeouts, and cap response size.

findings.title: PollFeed crashes on feed items without content and one bad item aborts the whole import
findings.body: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` raises NoMethodError when an RSS/Atom item has no content element (common for summary-only feeds; SimpleRSS may return nil or a different field such as description/summary). Because there is no per-item rescue, the exception aborts poll_feed mid-loop, so all remaining items are never imported and the hourly job fails on every run for such a feed. Guard nil content (fall back to description/summary) and isolate failures per item.

findings.title: Spec expects TopicRetriever in controller but implementation enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic
findings.body: The 'tells the topic retriever to work' example stubs/expects TopicRetriever.new and retriever.retrieve, but EmbedController#best at app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 instead calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...). TopicRetriever is never referenced by the controller, so this expectation fails (Jobs.enqueue is not stubbed and may enqueue a real job). The test as shipped does not pass against the implementation and does not verify the RetrieveTopic job arguments; update it to expect Jobs.enqueue with user_id/embed_url.

findings.title: import mutates caller's contents string and interpolates unescaped URL into HTML
findings.body: `contents << "...#{url}..."` mutates the string passed by the caller (raising FrozenError for frozen literals and corrupting reused strings, e.g. feed item content reused on retry), and the URL is interpolated unescaped into a single-quoted href attribute. A URL containing a quote can break out of the attribute and inject markup into the raw-HTML post. Duplicate the contents string first and HTML-escape/attribute-escape the URL when building the imported-from link.

findings.title: Disqus import silently drops the --category option and now requires fetching each thread URL
findings.body: The change removes the documented `method_option :category` (breaking existing invocations that pass -c, which Thor will now reject/ignore) and replaces local PostCreator creation with TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...), which performs a live HTTP fetch of each Disqus thread link. If a link is dead, redirects, or the site is offline, post becomes nil and all comments for that thread are silently skipped, whereas previously the topic was created locally from the export data. Preserve category support or document its removal, and fall back to creating the topic from export data when the remote fetch fails.
